entries.title: Halloween Costumes
entries.text: SHOW OFF YOUR SPOOKTACULAR STYLE! Get ready to bring your Halloween spirit to life with our Halloween Costume Contest! Whether you’re dressing up with your friends, showing off a one-of-a-kind creation, or stepping into the shoes of your favorite fictional character, this is your chance to show off your creativity and Halloween spirit! Start planning your costumes, gather your crew, and get ready to show off your Halloween spirit. Meet us on the Pā during lunch this Friday 10/30. The contest will begin promptly at 12:35, after the Orchestra is done playing. Contest Categories: Best Group Costume — Team up with your friends and coordinate your looks! Most Creative Costume — Bring your most original and imaginative ideas to life! Best Faculty/Staff Costume — Let’s see what our teachers and staff have up their sleeves! Best Fictional Character Costume — Become your favorite character from any work of fiction, whether it’s a book, movie, TV show, or beyond! Culture is Not a Costume- Halloween Dress Code Strictly Enforced (The Respect Rule) You must practice Cultural Appreciation, not Cultural Appropriation. What to Avoid: Do not wear clothing, hairstyles, or sacred symbols from a culture you do not belong to as a costume. This reinforces stereotypes and shows disrespect. Examples to Skip: Wearing a coconut bra and grass skirt, which mocks sacred Hawaiian culture. Dressing up in traditional garments from any culture (like Japanese, Egyptian, or African attire) if you don't belong to it and don't understand its meaning. What to Support: It's okay to wear something that honors your own ethnic heritage (like celebrating Dia De Los Muertos). Check Yourself (T.R.U.E.): Before you wear it, ask yourself: Tradition: Am I truly honoring the culture's history? Respect: Am I showing respect? Understanding: Do I understand the cultural context of my costume? Am I perpetuating historical stereotypes that further marginalized a group? Empathy: Would members of that culture feel valued if they saw me wearing this? Bottom Line: If your choice contains objectification for the purpose of a costume, it is not permitted. Choose a costume that values fun, not disrespect.
